KeePass. It's what I've used for years.

The only difference I've seen (other than the file extension) is that KeePassX doesn't have the ability to show your passwords. I guess the truly paranoid would see that as a good thing, but sometimes I don't want / need to use autotype (or I'm using KeePass on my phone when I'm trying to log into something on a friend's computer) and I just want to see my password.
A quick Google search shows they are essentially the same application. KeePass was originally Windows-only and KeePassX was the cross-platform version. Now the original is also cross-platform.
What features does that have? How it "works"?

It stores all of your passwords in a password protected (I think encrypted) file. You can also set up keyfiles to make it so that even if someone gets your "master" password, they still can't open the file and see all of your passwords. The nicest feature is that it has an auto-type option so you can alt-tab from the login screen to KeePass, right-click and select auto-type, then it alt-tabs back to your browser / other program and types in your user name, then tabs down and enters the password, then hits enter for you. I keep my KeePass files on Dropbox so I can access the same file on my desktop, laptop, or phone.
I pay for LastPass because it's worth it and not that expensive. It's a good service, why not pay a few bucks for it?

Absolutely, I'm a premium customer myself and their pricing so far has been more than reasonable. But in addition to cancelling their free options, LogMeIn also has a history of jacking up prices and removing features from lower tiers of their subscription plans. I'll give them the benefit of the doubt, but will not be renewing my subscription if they do this to LastPass as well.

I paid for a year of LastPass, but I've honestly started questioning whether it's worth it or not. The number of things I need to log into on my phone can be counted on one hand, and with that quantity I can deal with something like KeePass. Not to mention KeePass keeps my passwords in my hands only. Sure, it takes some extra work to keep things synced, but they're also much more secure, too.

LogMeIn was great until they made it pay-only. If they do the same with LastPass, you can be sure they will be overshadowed by a free alternative.
